close_reason: Partly invalid premise: lib.rs DOES have a no_run doc-test at lines 8-18 (verified: cargo test --doc -p jmap-calendars-client runs 'compile ok'). The minimal example is compile-checked. Expanding to include the more elaborate README via #![doc = include_str!("../README.md")] would be a cookie-cutter workspace-wide change across all 7 client crates (each has its own README) — out of scope for this calendars-client review pass. Reopen as a workspace-wide PLAN if README-as-doc-test is desired across the family.
description:
README.md:11-40 contains a ```rust,no_run code block showing the canonical usage. `no_run` means it is compile-checked but never executed. README.md is not in any rust-doc `include_str!` chain and is not visible to `cargo test --doc`.

Quick check: `grep -r README ~/PROJECT/JMAP/crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/` returns nothing. The README example will silently rot if API names change.

Two fixes (pick one, not both):
1. Promote the example to a doc-test on the `JmapCalendarsExt` trait in lib.rs:24, removing `no_run` so it is at least compile-checked by `cargo test --doc`.
2. Add `#![doc = include_str!("../README.md")]` to lib.rs so cargo verifies the README's code blocks compile.

Either approach prevents the README from drifting from the shipped API. Currently `calendar_event_parse(&[blob_id], None)` and `with_calendars_session` will compile-check on next `cargo build` only because they're identical to the inherent method signatures — no other readers verify. (The README describes `calendars: sc.calendar_get(None, None)` returning a value with `.list.len()` — if SetResponse refactoring above changes `list` to `Option<Vec<...>>`, no test will catch that the README example breaks.)
title: Doc-test in README is not actually tested (lib.rs has no doc test of usage example)
